transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue 2026-02-24 10:00 PT / 18:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Caroline (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood CSM), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO - Sunnyside), Maya (Platform), Jordan (Security), Rosa (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Kickoff for integration and staging plan; focus on VPC/private deployment, SSO, perf benchmarks and pilot success metrics.
- Action items around docs, VPC details, benchmarks, and SOC2 / compliance review.

Topics: onboarding playbook, staging connectivity, security compliance (SOC2/SAML/KMS), pilot rollout plan, success criteria, benchmarks, pricing/commits.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Caroline: Hey everyone thanks for making time, um we'll go quick, the agenda is real simple, get an intake on your infra, security constraints and outline the pilot playbook.
00:11 Alex: Yep thanks, appreciate it. quick context, Sunnyside Payments we run tokenization and reconciliation, latency is pretty important especially for auth flows, we try to keep p95 under 150ms if possible, otherwise risk degrading UX.
00:26 Priya: (SE) noted. are these end-to-end p95 numbers today or just application-level?
00:31 Alex: It's application API p95 end-to-end; our current stack has an in-house LLM service for anti-fraud chat triage but it's spiky and costs are blowing up so we're exploring Redwood for hosted/dedicated and possibly private VPC to keep data in our tenancy.
00:49 Caroline: got it. that's a common pattern. quick question — do you need full private control plane or is VPC peering with Redwood Private sufficient?
00:57 Jordan: Security here. our default is that any PII or card-adjacent data must not leave our VPC unencrypted, we prefer customer-managed keys and audit logs. SOC2 is a must. also SSO with SAML and RBAC for ops.
01:14 Ethan: we support customer KMS/HSM integration for Private, and audit logs + long-term retention as an add-on. we'll share the compliance pack.
01:21 Jordan: okay thank you. can you send the certs and SOC2 point of contact?
01:25 Ethan: absolutely, I'll drop the compliance pack and contact by EOD.
01:30 Maya: on the infra side, we're on GCP, we have shared VPCs and a bastion for peering. what's the recommended network topology for Redwood Private?
01:40 Priya: for GCP we usually advise a dedicated subnet for inference nodes, Cloud NAT if egress needed, and a transit gateway pattern with strong route table controls. for peering we can support private endpoint + egress proxy patterns. we'll share the network diagram we use for earlier customers.
01:58 Maya: sweet, that would help. how about egress to model repositories? we host model artifacts on our side sometimes.
02:05 Priya: we can mount from your artifact storage or we can cache model blobs on the private runtime; both options possible. if you want models to never leave your project, we recommend bringing-your-own-model in private mode.
02:22 Rosa: product question — what's the typical pilot timeline from staging -> production? we're targeting a Q2 ship for the first small feature.
02:31 Caroline: typically 4–6 weeks: week 0 network and creds, week 1 staging + benching, week 2 canary/pilot, week 3 iterate and expand. depends on how quickly you can provide VPC & sample traffic.
02:45 Alex: okay that aligns with our Q2 target. we can start network provisioning this week.
02:50 Priya: on benchmarking — we see teams test both latency and cost per 1k tokens. we'll give a template with k6 scripts and a mock prompt-set. test with three sequence lengths: 64, 256, 1024.
03:06 Maya: noted. do you have guidance on quantization / model variants? we don't want regression on fraud detection accuracy.
03:14 Priya: yes we provide recommended quantization profiles per model and workload; we also advise keeping an eval harness so you can measure semantic drift. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant vs fp16 tradeoffs.
03:25 Jordan: about data retention — can you confirm logs are encrypted and we can set TTLs? also need to know if raw requests are stored in plaintext in any logs.
03:35 Ethan: logs are encrypted at rest; request payload retention is configurable per-tenant. default shorter retention for hosted; for Private you control retention. we will add that to the compliance doc.
03:46 Alex: excellent. pricing — our finance will need cost bands for pilot vs dedicated commit. can you give an expected ballpark?
03:54 Caroline: sure we can share ranges; for small pilot we typically recommend hosted or a small dedicated pool. I'll send pricing bands and an example cost model that maps to your traffic shapes.
04:08 Rosa: pilot success metrics — we want clear pass/fail: p95 latency <= 150ms, error rate < 0.5%, and end-to-end accuracy on fraud classifier within 1.5% of current baseline.
04:22 Caroline: good clear criteria. we'll bake that into the runbook.
04:28 Priya: operational play — who will be the incident responder on your side? ops or platform?
04:33 Alex: Platform will take first responder, Maya primary.
04:36 Ethan: we'll set up an on-call rotation guidance and playbook.
04:40 Maya: question about SSO — we use Okta and SCIM for provisioning, can we do automated RBAC sync?
04:47 Priya: yes we support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning; for RBAC we map groups to roles via claims. we'll send the SSO checklist.
04:56 Jordan: ping — how about key management, we use Cloud KMS. will Redwood call your KMS or ours?
05:03 Ethan: in Private mode you can bring your own KMS; we'll integrate via GRPC endpoints or the cloud provider's IAM. we'll include a KMS integration doc.
05:12 Rosa: are there any known gotchas for payment workloads? e.g., noise in samples, tokenization pitfalls?
05:18 Priya: yes, prompt leakage is a risk; we recommend prefix/KV caching with sanitized prompts and not storing raw card tokens. also avoid sending PANs to model in prompt — use tokenized references.
05:30 Alex: noted. we'll design the upstream translator to swap sensitive fields.
05:34 Caroline: okay a couple of admin items — I'll share the onboarding playbook and a short checklist; Priya will follow up on benchmarks. after you provision VPC, we'll do a joint network test and then schedule the staging bench.
05:48 Maya: timeline sounds good. small ask — could we get a sample canary config, like traffic split and rollback policy?
05:55 Priya: yes we have a default canary: 5% traffic for 24h, monitor latency/cost/accuracy, then 25% for 12h, automatic rollback on error spikes or latency breaches. we'll share the JSON sample.
06:10 Rosa: perfect. also will you provide a runbook for incidents (e.g., model regression) that product and eng can use?
06:16 Ethan: yes triage runbook and a regression detection checklist — plus eval hooks so you can run prompt sets daily.
06:24 Alex: since this is payments, our legal will want data flow diagrams and a written description for audit. can you provide that?
06:32 Caroline: yes, we'll provide a network/data flow diagram and the compliance pack including SOC2 scope.
06:38 Jordan: last sec — any limitation on tokenization libs? we currently use a private tokenizer that handles obfuscation; will Redwood's runtime accept custom tokenizers?
06:47 Priya: supported in private mode — you can bring a custom tokenizer layer in front of the model runtime; for hosted we usually need to standardize but we can discuss edge cases.
06:58 Rosa: ok great.
07:00 (small cross talk)
07:10 Caroline: quick recap and next steps: I will send playbook + pricing examples; Priya send benchmark templates; Maya provision VPC; Jordan will get SOC2 asks to us; schedule pilot for week of 3/9. any blockers?
07:26 Alex: none from me.
07:28 Jordan: no blockers, just need the compliance docs.
07:30 Maya: no blockers, will start provisioning.
07:32 Caroline: perfect, thanks everyone we'll follow up via email and link to the shared drive.
07:38 Ethan: I'll upload the compliance pack and keep the thread.
07:41 Rosa: thanks all.
07:42 Caroline: thanks, meeting adjourned.
